NEGOTIATION NOTES – WASL / ABT
Vessel Call Fees & Service Adjustments
File Ref: WASL-ABT/NN/2019-2023
Location: Apapa, Lagos

Note 1 – 14 March 2019
Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL Commercial), A. Bello (ABT Ports), T. Adeyemi (WASL Ops)
Subject: Review of current call fee structure and service level expectations for the 2019-2020 tariff year.

Discussion:
- ABT confirmed that the current per-call fee for West Africa Shipping Lines stands at 45000 USD. West Africa Shipping Lines vessel_call_fee_per_call 45000 USD. Record status: historical. This was noted as the baseline for all further discussions.
- WASL raised concerns about the frequency of draft surveys, particularly for vessels arriving at night. ABT explained that night surveys attract an overtime surcharge which is billed separately, not within the call fee.
- ABT proposed a review of the bundling of pilotage and towage in the call fee. WASL asked for a breakdown of the service components to understand what is actually covered.
- Both parties agreed that any adjustment to the fee would require a minimum of 90 days notice before implementation, and that the current rate remains in effect until a new agreement is signed.

Action Items:
1. ABT to provide a detailed breakdown of services covered by the call fee by 28 March 2019.
2. WASL to share vessel call volume projections for the next 12 months.
3. Both parties to schedule a follow-up meeting in April 2019.

Next Meeting: 18 April 2019, 10:00 AM WAT, ABT Head Office, Lagos.

Note 2 – 18 April 2019
Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL), A. Bello (ABT), M. Ibrahim (ABT Finance)
Subject: Service breakdown and preliminary feedback on fee adjustment.

Discussion:
- ABT presented the service breakdown. The call fee covers berthing, unberthing, and basic port dues. It does not include cargo handling, pilotage, or towage, which are billed separately.
- WASL noted that this differs from the understanding at the March meeting, where pilotage and towage were thought to be bundled. ABT clarified that this was a misunderstanding and the breakdown has always been as presented.
- WASL requested a copy of the 2018 tariff schedule for comparison. ABT said they would share it.
- ABT mentioned that they are considering a 5% increase in the call fee for the next tariff year, but no final decision has been made. WASL pushed back, stating that service levels need to improve first, particularly around turnaround times.

Action Items:
1. ABT to share the 2018 tariff schedule by 30 April 2019.
2. WASL to provide data on average turnaround times for their vessels.
3. ABT to prepare a draft proposal for the 2020 tariff year by end of May.

Next Meeting: 20 June 2019, 11:00 AM WAT.

Note 3 – 20 June 2019
Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL), A. Bello (ABT), T. Adeyemi (WASL Ops), J. Eze (ABT Legal)
Subject: Draft proposal for 2020 tariff year.

Discussion:
- ABT presented the draft proposal. It includes a 5% increase in the call fee, effective 1 January 2020. WASL noted that this would bring the fee to 47250 USD, but the discussion was not concluded.
- WASL argued that the increase is not justified given the current service levels. They cited instances of delayed berthing due to equipment failure at the port.
- ABT responded that the increase is necessary to fund infrastructure upgrades, including new bollards and fenders.
- WASL requested a clause in the agreement that allows for a mid-year review if service levels do not meet agreed benchmarks.
- ABT Legal said they would review the request and come back with language.
Note 4 – 23 September 2019
Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL), A. Bello (ABT), M. Ibrahim (ABT Finance), T. Adeyemi (WASL Ops)
Subject: Mid-year review clause and tariff schedule comparison.

Discussion:
- ABT Legal circulated draft language for the mid-year review clause. WASL reviewed and asked for two changes: (i) the review to be triggered by any two consecutive months of missed turnaround benchmarks, not just one; and (ii) the review outcome to allow for a rebate, not only a deferral of the increase.
- ABT said the rebate option is difficult because tariffs are set annually by the port authority framework. They suggested a service credit against future ancillary charges instead. WASL agreed to consider this.
- The 2018 tariff schedule was shared. WASL compared it with the 2020 draft. The main difference is the proposed 5% increase; the structure of charges is otherwise unchanged. WASL asked why the 2018 schedule shows a separate line for "port infrastructure levy" that does not appear in the 2020 draft. ABT Finance said the levy was folded into the basic port dues line during a reclassification in early 2019. WASL requested written confirmation of this reclassification.
- WASL provided turnaround data for their vessels for January to August 2019. Average was 14.6 hours, above the 12-hour benchmark. ABT acknowledged the data but noted that two incidents were due to weather and one to a vessel-side mechanical issue.

Action Items:
1. ABT Legal to revise the mid-year review clause to include the two-consecutive-month trigger and the service credit option.
2. ABT Finance to provide written confirmation of the levy reclassification by 7 October 2019.
3. WASL to confirm whether they accept the service credit approach in principle.

Next Meeting: 24 October 2019, 10:00 AM WAT.

Note 5 – 24 October 2019
Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL), A. Bello (ABT), J. Eze (ABT Legal)
Subject: Clause language and 2020 tariff confirmation.

Discussion:

- ABT confirmed the 2020 tariff year will proceed with the 5% increase as drafted. WASL noted this is without prejudice to the mid-year review. ABT agreed.
- WASL asked about the effective date for the new tariff. ABT confirmed 1 January 2020. Invoicing for vessels arriving before that date will be at the 2019 rate even if the vessel is still in port after 1 January.
- ABT Finance’s written confirmation of the levy reclassification was received on 8 October. WASL said they would review and come back if there are questions.

2. ABT to issue a formal notice of the 2020 tariff to all shipping lines by 15 November 2019.
3. Both parties to agree on turnaround benchmark reporting format for the mid-year review.

Note 6 – 19 November 2019
Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL), A. Bello (ABT), T. Adeyemi (WASL Ops), M. Ibrahim (ABT Finance)
Subject: Finalisation of 2020 agreement.

Discussion:
- WASL Legal confirmed acceptance of the mid-year review clause. The agreement for the 2020 tariff year is now considered final.

- The parties agreed to a quarterly reporting format for turnaround times. ABT will provide monthly data to WASL Ops, and a joint review will be held every three months starting April 2020.

This report presents the findings of the compliance audit of port operations conducted by
Maritime Compliance Services Ltd at the Lagos Port complex (Apapa and Tin Can Island
terminals) during the period under review. The audit assessed operational compliance with
the LPA Port Operations Manual (2021 edition), the Nigerian Ports Authority Act (Cap.
N126, LFN 2004), and applicable international maritime safety conventions as adopted by
the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA).

The audit covered five operational areas: cargo handling safety, vessel berthing
documentation, waste management and pollution control, security access control, and
maintenance of port infrastructure. A total of twenty-four (24) findings were recorded,
comprising nine (9) high-risk, eleven (11) medium-risk, and four (4) low-risk items.

Management has provided responses to each finding. Thirteen (13) findings have been
remediated as at the date of this report, and eleven (11) remain open. The open findings
require immediate management attention, particularly those rated high-risk.

2.0 AUDIT SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY

The audit was conducted between 15 September 2022 and 28 October 2022. The audit team
reviewed operational logs, interviewed terminal supervisors and safety officers, observed
cargo handling operations during day and night shifts, and inspected physical infrastructure
including quay walls, bollards, fenders, and lighting towers.

The audit was performed in accordance with the International Standards for the
Professional Practice of Internal Auditing (IPPF) and the MCS Audit Field Manual (Rev. 4).

4.1 LPA-2022-01: Insufficient fall protection on container gantry cranes

Risk Rating: High
Status: Open
Target Remediation Date: 31 January 2023

Finding: During the inspection of Quay 3 and Quay 5, the audit team observed that harness anchor points on two of the six post-Panamax gantry cranes (Crane 4 and Crane 6) did not meet the manufacturer's specification. The existing anchor points were found to be corroded and, in one instance, the locking mechanism failed to engage during a simulated drop test. This condition exposes maintenance personnel to fall hazards from heights exceeding 30 metres when performing routine servicing of the spreader and trolley systems.

Applicable Requirement: International Labour Organization (ILO) Convention No. 152, Section 4.2; LPA Safety Manual, Chapter 7, Clause 7.3.1.

Management Response (received 18 November 2022, signed by Chief Engineer, Terminal Operations): The Port Engineering Department acknowledges the finding. A procurement request for replacement anchor points has been submitted to the stores unit. We have also engaged the original equipment manufacturer to provide a revised installation drawing. Temporary lanyard points have been marked and are being used by the maintenance crew pending full rectification.

Auditor's Comment: The temporary lanyard points are not a permanent substitute. The audit team will verify the installation of the new anchor points and the results of the drop test during the follow-up visit.

4.2 LPA-2022-02: Inadequate segregation and storage of hazardous waste

Risk Rating: High
Status: Open
Target Remediation Date: 15 December 2022

Finding: The waste collection point adjacent to the container freight station was found to contain used lubricating oil drums stored alongside general municipal waste. The oil drums were not placed in a bunded area and lacked secondary containment. A review of the waste manifest for September and October 2022 indicates that 14 drums of used oil were collected, but only 6 were recorded as transferred to the licensed disposal contractor. The discrepancy was not explained by the operations log.

Applicable Requirement: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) Guidelines on Hazardous Waste Management; LPA Waste Management Procedure, Section 5.2.

Management Response (received 25 November 2022, signed by the Environmental Officer): The waste collection point is due for an upgrade. A bunded concrete slab and a covered storage cage have been budgeted for the 2023 capital programme. In the interim, the operations supervisor has been directed to separate the oil drums and move them to a temporary location behind the workshop. The missing 8 drums were traced to a spillage that occurred during loading; the oil was absorbed with sand and the contaminated sand was disposed of as hazardous waste. Supporting documentation is attached.

Auditor's Comment: The explanation for the 8 drums is noted. The audit team requests a copy of the disposal certificate for the contaminated sand. The physical relocation of the drums does not meet the requirement for secondary containment. This finding will be re-tested in December 2022.

4.5 LPA-2022-05: Deterioration of pavement on access road to Berth 9

Risk Rating: Medium
Status: Open
Target Remediation Date: 28 February 2023

Finding: The access road serving Berth 9, used primarily by refrigerated container trucks, exhibits significant potholing and edge failure over a stretch of approximately 120 metres. The condition is causing trucks to slow to less than 5 km/h, and there are reports of damage to reefer units due to vibration. The audit team observed that the drainage channels adjacent to the road are blocked with silt, which is contributing to water pooling and further degradation of the sub-base.

Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL Commercial), A. Bello (ABT Ports), T. Adeyemi (WASL Ops)
Subject: Review of current call fee structure and service level expectations for the 2019-2020 tariff year.

Discussion:
- ABT confirmed that the current per-call fee for West Africa Shipping Lines stands at 45000 USD. West Africa Shipping Lines vessel_call_fee_per_call 45000 USD. Record status: historical. This was noted as the baseline for all further discussions.
- WASL raised concerns about the frequency of draft surveys, particularly for vessels arriving at night. ABT explained that night surveys attract an overtime surcharge which is billed separately, not within the call fee.
- ABT proposed a review of the bundling of pilotage and towage in the call fee. WASL asked for a breakdown of the service components to understand what is actually covered.
- Both parties agreed that any adjustment to the fee would require a minimum of 90 days notice before implementation, and that the current rate remains in effect until a new agreement is signed.

Action Items:
1. ABT to provide a detailed breakdown of services covered by the call fee by 28 March 2019.
2. WASL to share vessel call volume projections for the next 12 months.
3. Both parties to schedule a follow-up meeting in April 2019.

Next Meeting: 18 April 2019, 10:00 AM WAT, ABT Head Office, Lagos.

Note 2 – 18 April 2019
Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL), A. Bello (ABT), M. Ibrahim (ABT Finance)
Subject: Service breakdown and preliminary feedback on fee adjustment.

Discussion:
- ABT presented the service breakdown. The call fee covers berthing, unberthing, and basic port dues. It does not include cargo handling, pilotage, or towage, which are billed separately.
- WASL noted that this differs from the understanding at the March meeting, where pilotage and towage were thought to be bundled. ABT clarified that this was a misunderstanding and the breakdown has always been as presented.
- WASL requested a copy of the 2018 tariff schedule for comparison. ABT said they would share it.
- ABT mentioned that they are considering a 5% increase in the call fee for the next tariff year, but no final decision has been made. WASL pushed back, stating that service levels need to improve first, particularly around turnaround times.

Action Items:
1. ABT to share the 2018 tariff schedule by 30 April 2019.
2. WASL to provide data on average turnaround times for their vessels.
3. ABT to prepare a draft proposal for the 2020 tariff year by end of May.

Next Meeting: 20 June 2019, 11:00 AM WAT.

Note 3 – 20 June 2019
Attendees: C. Okafor (WASL), A. Bello (ABT), T. Adeyemi (WASL Ops), J. Eze (ABT Legal)
Subject: Draft proposal for 2020 tariff year.

Discussion:
- ABT presented the draft proposal. It includes a 5% increase in the call fee, effective 1 January 2020. WASL noted that this would bring the fee to 47250 USD, but the discussion was not concluded.
- WASL argued that the increase is not justified given the current service levels. They cited instances of delayed berthing due to equipment failure at the port.
- ABT responded that the increase is necessary to fund infrastructure upgrades, including new bollards and fenders.
- WASL requested a clause in the agreement that allows for a mid-year review if service levels do not meet agreed benchmarks.
- ABT Legal said they would review the request and come back with language.

Subject: Mid-year review clause and tariff schedule comparison.

- ABT Legal circulated draft language for the mid-year review clause. WASL asked why the 2018 schedule shows a separate line for "port infrastructure levy" that does not appear in the 2020 draft. ABT Finance said the levy was folded into the basic port dues line during a reclassification in early 2019. WASL requested written confirmation of this reclassification.
- WASL provided turnaround data for their vessels for January to August 2019. Average was 14.6 hours, above the 12-hour benchmark. ABT acknowledged the data but noted that two incidents were due to weather and one to a vessel-side mechanical issue.

documents.content:
4.1 LPA-2022-01: Insufficient fall protection on container gantry cranes

Risk Rating: High
Status: Open
Target Remediation Date: 31 January 2023

Finding: During the inspection of Quay 3 and Quay 5, the audit team observed that harness anchor points on two of the six post-Panamax gantry cranes (Crane 4 and Crane 6) did not meet the manufacturer's specification. The existing anchor points were found to be corroded and, in one instance, the locking mechanism failed to engage during a simulated drop test. This condition exposes maintenance personnel to fall hazards from heights exceeding 30 metres when performing routine servicing of the spreader and trolley systems.

Applicable Requirement: International Labour Organization (ILO) Convention No. 152, Section 4.2; LPA Safety Manual, Chapter 7, Clause 7.3.1.

Management Response (received 18 November 2022, signed by Chief Engineer, Terminal Operations): The Port Engineering Department acknowledges the finding. A procurement request for replacement anchor points has been submitted to the stores unit. We have also engaged the original equipment manufacturer to provide a revised installation drawing. Temporary lanyard points have been marked and are being used by the maintenance crew pending full rectification.

Auditor's Comment: The temporary lanyard points are not a permanent substitute. The audit team will verify the installation of the new anchor points and the results of the drop test during the follow-up visit.

---

4.2 LPA-2022-02: Inadequate segregation and storage of hazardous waste

Risk Rating: High
Status: Open
Target Remediation Date: 15 December 2022

Finding: The waste collection point adjacent to the container freight station was found to contain used lubricating oil drums stored alongside general municipal waste. The oil drums were not placed in a bunded area and lacked secondary containment. A review of the waste manifest for September and October 2022 indicates that 14 drums of used oil were collected, but only 6 were recorded as transferred to the licensed disposal contractor. The discrepancy was not explained by the operations log.

Applicable Requirement: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) Guidelines on Hazardous Waste Management; LPA Waste Management Procedure, Section 5.2.

Management Response (received 25 November 2022, signed by the Environmental Officer): The waste collection point is due for an upgrade. A bunded concrete slab and a covered storage cage have been budgeted for the 2023 capital programme. In the interim, the operations supervisor has been directed to separate the oil drums and move them to a temporary location behind the workshop. The missing 8 drums were traced to a spillage that occurred during loading; the oil was absorbed with sand and the contaminated sand was disposed of as hazardous waste. Supporting documentation is attached.

Auditor's Comment: The explanation for the 8 drums is noted. The audit team requests a copy of the disposal certificate for the contaminated sand. The physical relocation of the drums does not meet the requirement for secondary containment. This finding will be re-tested in December 2022.

---

4.5 LPA-2022-05: Deterioration of pavement on access road to Berth 9

Risk Rating: Medium
Status: Open
Target Remediation Date: 28 February 2023

Finding: The access road serving Berth 9, used primarily by refrigerated container trucks, exhibits significant potholing and edge failure over a stretch of approximately 120 metres. The condition is causing trucks to slow to less than 5 km/h, and there are reports of damage to reefer units due to vibration. The audit team observed that the drainage channels adjacent to the road are blocked with silt, which is contributing to water pooling and further degradation of the sub-base.

SECTION I: PAYMENT PROCEDURES AND GENERAL CONDITIONS

1. All charges set out in this Tariff Schedule shall be paid in United States Dollars (USD) or in Naira at the official Central Bank of Nigeria exchange rate prevailing on the date of payment, unless otherwise directed by the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) in writing.

2. Payment shall be made by electronic transfer into the designated NPA revenue account. Cheques shall not be accepted for port charges except where a prior arrangement has been approved in writing by the General Manager, Finance.

3. Vessels shall not be granted inward or outward clearance until all applicable charges under this Schedule have been settled or satisfactory security for payment has been provided to the satisfaction of the Port Manager.

4. Where a vessel or cargo owner disputes a charge, a written notice of dispute must be submitted to the Port Manager within fourteen (14) days of the charge being raised. Pending resolution of the dispute, the disputed amount shall be paid under protest and shall be subject to refund with interest at the prevailing Central Bank of Nigeria monetary policy rate should the dispute be determined in favour of the payer.

5. All administrative charges under Section H are non-refundable except where the charge was levied in error or where the service for which the charge was paid is not provided due to a default by the NPA.

6. Port users shall be entitled to a receipt for every payment made. Receipts shall be issued electronically and shall bear the unique transaction reference number generated at the point of payment.

7. Where a vessel remains at berth beyond the free time allowed under the relevant terminal agreement, demurrage charges shall be levied in accordance with the terminal operator's published schedule and the provisions of Section F of this Tariff.

8. The NPA reserves the right to revise any rate or charge contained in this Schedule upon thirty (30) days' public notice published in at least two national newspapers and on the NPA official website.
